# oxframe

oxframe is procedural animation in Rust. Scenes are async functions; awaiting an animation takes time.

This is oxframe 0.2.1, pre-1.0: the API is not stable and changes between versions. Pin the exact version and follow these docs for it, not model memory.

Full text: https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/llms-full.txt

## Start here

- [Welcome](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1): Learn oxframe: make animations and motion graphics by writing Rust code, with a live editor to scrub through them and fine-tune the timing.
- [Install and first project](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/getting-started): Install the oxframe CLI with cargo, create your first animation project and open the live editor — five minutes from nothing to a moving scene.

## Guide

- [1. Your first animation](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/hello): Lesson 1 of the oxframe guide: add a circle to the screen and animate it with Rust. The basic pattern behind every animation, with a live example.
- [2. In order, or all at once](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/together): Lesson 2: run animations one after another or all at once with sequence, all and delays — composing timing in Rust with oxframe.
- [3. Shapes, colors, transforms](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/shapes): Lesson 3: rectangles, circles, lines and polygons; fills and outlines; rotation, scale and color — the properties every oxframe shape shares.
- [4. Easing](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/easing): Lesson 4: easing curves explained — why some animations feel natural and others robotic, and how to pick the right ease-in and ease-out curve.
- [5. Text](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/text): Lesson 5: animate text in Rust — titles, typewriter effects, mixed styles and syntax-highlighted code blocks with oxframe.
- [6. Groups and layout](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/groups): Lesson 6: nest shapes in groups and let flexbox-style layout arrange them, so whole compositions move and scale together.
- [7. Tweak timing in the editor](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/editor): Lesson 7: adjust timing by eye in the oxframe editor — markers, eases and tunables you can drag without touching or recompiling code.
- [8. Signals](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/signals): Lesson 8: signals make one value follow another — a line that always connects two dots, a label that always shows a number.
- [9. Drawing and morphing](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/drawing): Lesson 9: draw an outline as if with a pen, then morph one shape into another — path drawing and shape morphing in oxframe.
- [10. Randomness and background tasks](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/guide/random): Lesson 10: background tasks and seeded randomness — many things moving on their own while the story continues, rendering the same video every time.

## Going further

- [All nodes](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/nodes): Reference of every oxframe node and its properties: Rect, Circle, Line, Path, Polygon, Star, Txt, Code, Img, Layout and Grid.
- [Effects](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/effects): Gradients, dashes, shadows, blur, blend modes and clipping in oxframe. Every effect is a signal and animates like any other property.
- [Markers, eases, tunables](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/timing): Markers, custom eases and tunables: timing values stored outside your Rust code so you can adjust them visually in the oxframe editor.
- [The editor](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/editor): A tour of the oxframe editor: viewport, timeline, inspector and hot reload — the same app in oxframe dev and in the browser playground.
- [Rendering video](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/rendering): Render oxframe animations to MP4, WebM with alpha, ProRes 4444 or PNG sequences with one command, on the GPU or CPU, with audio.
- [CLI reference](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/cli): Reference for the oxframe command line: init, dev, render, snapshot, check, agents and upgrade, with all options.
- [Working with AI agents](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/agents): Use Claude Code, Codex or Cursor to write oxframe animations: every project ships agent instructions and a way for agents to see what they made.

## Under the hood

- [How oxframe works](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.2.1/how-it-works): How oxframe works inside: scenes as Rust coroutines, deterministic rendering, instant scrubbing, and compiling Rust to WebAssembly for the browser.
